problems.description: @types/handlebars is a deprecated stub package (handlebars 4.7.9 ships its own types) and is installed into 'dependencies' — type packages belong in devDependencies; this adds a redundant, deprecated prod dependency.

handlebars plus its transitive deps (minimist, neo-async, source-map, uglify-js, wordwrap) were moved from devDependencies into the production dependency tree, widening the runtime surface of the published CLI; if handlebars is only used at build/generate time this misclassification should be reverted.

Mechanical convention score is 0.49 with casing violations (snake_case functions, non-PascalCase classes, non-UPPER_CASE constants). Discrepancy flagged: the named offending files (custom-plugin.example.ts, index.ts, cli.test.ts) are not part of this diff, so the score likely reflects pre-existing worktree state — but the new +11 functions/+112 imports should be checked for the same conventions.
New test code adds +8 smells, +23 cognitive complexity, and +4.0% duplication — the repeated mkdir/writeFileSync/rmSync scaffolding in each test could be extracted into shared helpers.

strengths: On-domain feature: adding Handlebars templating to a static site generator fits the project's purpose.
Comprehensive test coverage for the new feature (template dir, custom template, custom layout cases) with proper beforeEach/afterEach cleanup so tests don't leak files.
New tests follow the existing test file's filesystem-based pattern rather than introducing a new testing approach.

problems.description: Convention score 0.49 with 84 violations across the commit (custom-plugin.example.ts, index.ts, cli.test.ts): classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE, functions using snake_case instead of camelCase.

Test body is heavily repetitive — every case re-declares the same temp dirs, file writes, and SiteGenerator construction instead of using helpers or parameterized setup; SonarQube flags +14 smells and +44 cognitive complexity, mostly from this duplication.

Tests create/remove fixtures under __dirname (incremental-test-content/output). Cleanup is present in beforeEach/afterEach, but a crash mid-run leaves stale state that could mask or contaminate later runs.

bugs +0 and duplication -2.3% — the change is functionally sound and reduces overall duplication.

commit_reviews.summary: A functionally complete, API-driven test suite for incremental builds that lands cleanly (bugs 0, duplication down) but drags the convention score to 0.49 via 84 naming violations and accumulates test duplication that SonarQube flags as +14 smells / +44 cognitive complexity.

compounding_issues: Session 1 committed node_modules (5152 files, ~969k insertions) and dist/ with no .gitignore; none was ever added, so every later commit diff is polluted with dependency and build-artifact noise.

The bad_seed (0.5) delivered a mismatched Express/JWT auth-API seed (200-line index.ts) unrelated to the SSG story, so session 1 had to build effectively greenfield and the seed never informed the architecture.
EJS template support promised in the session-2 prompt was never implemented — the template engine and per-page `template` field are Handlebars/.hbs-only, so the stated scope was only half met.

The session-4 plugin refactor left coupling seams: DevServer reaches into SiteGenerator private fields via bracket access (this.generator['contentDir']), and SiteGenerator shares internal state with plugins (storeFrontmatter, markdownPlugin.getParsedContent) that bypasses the plugin's own onFile pipeline, making part of the plugin boundary cosmetic.
key_decisions: Discard the irrelevant auth-API seed and build the SSG cleanly greenfield in session 1 — the correct call under a mismatched bad_seed, resulting in clean modular types.ts / markdown-parser.ts / site-generator.ts / cli.ts.
Adopt Handlebars with layouts, partials, and compiled-template caching (session 2) as the template strategy.
Implement the live-reload dev server with ws + chokidar and wire `ssg serve` into the CLI (session 3).

Extract a lifecycle-hook plugin architecture (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd via PluginManager) and re-home markdown, template, and the dev server as plugins, with PLUGIN_SYSTEM.md and an example plugin (session 4).
Add incremental builds via a sha256 .ssg-cache.json manifest (CacheManager) exposed as --incremental/--clean CLI flags (session 5).
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality arcs upward across the five sessions. Session 1 laid a strong, well-tested foundation (7 source files, 610 test lines) and stayed disciplined by ignoring the mismatched seed. Session 2 cleanly extended with a cached template engine plus 237 new test lines. Session 3 added the dev server but was the weakest point — the lowest confidence (0.74), a monolithic 204-line module, and the smallest test delta. Session 4 was the pivotal, riskiest commit: a genuine refactor (844 insertions / 280 deletions) that split the generator into plugins and swapped the 204-line dev server for a plugin, backed by 329 test lines and docs, though it introduced the private-field and shared-state hacks that linger to the end. Session 5 closed strong with incremental builds/caching and 377 test lines integrated through the refactored pipeline. Tests were extended in every session and exit codes were clean throughout, so capability and coverage grew monotonically even as the session-4 restructuring temporarily thinned some seams.
story_review.summary: A coherent, well-paced feature→refactor→optimization arc that steadily improved — despite a mismatched bad seed, committed node_modules, and a partial EJS scope gap — culminating in a plugin-based SSG with templates, live reload, and incremental builds.
